items.title: India clinches T20I series in New Zealand after Abhishek Sharma's 113
items.text: India beat New Zealand by six wickets in the third T20 International in Wellington on 27 October, chasing a target of 199 in 13.2 overs. Abhishek Sharma scored 113 from 38 balls, reaching his century in 35 deliveries, while 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi made 45. The win gave India an unassailable 3–0 lead with two matches remaining.

items.title: Schools in eight Odisha districts scheduled to close as Cyclone Arnab approaches
items.text: Schools in eight Odisha districts were scheduled to remain closed on Wednesday, 28 October, as very severe Cyclone Arnab approached the east coast. The India Meteorological Department issued an orange alert for several districts and forecast 12–20 cm of rain in some areas. Authorities prepared evacuations and shelters; families were advised to follow official district notices for local closure and travel guidance.

items.title: Indian shares face a weaker opening as oil rises and Jio IPO draws attention
items.text: Reuters reported on 28 October that Indian shares were expected to open lower as rising oil prices weighed on investor sentiment ahead of the US Federal Reserve decision. Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion IPO attracted $77 billion in bids and was expected to make the company one of India's largest listed firms by market value. The report also noted a weaker GIFT Nifty indication.

items.title: Raghuram Rajan cautions India against using up reserves to defend a rupee level
items.text: Former Reserve Bank of India Governor Raghuram Rajan told Reuters that India should avoid exhausting foreign-exchange reserves to defend a specific rupee exchange rate. He said moderate depreciation can support exports, while high oil prices, US Treasury yields and foreign equity outflows have put pressure on the currency. He also warned that expensive oil can widen India's current-account deficit.

items.title: PM Modi highlights India's science and technology progress at New Delhi conclave
items.text: At a science conclave in New Delhi on Tuesday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised India's achievements in science and technology, describing the country as advancing with a new vision, a changed mindset and renewed self-confidence. The Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave brings researchers, policymakers, industry leaders and startups together to discuss emerging technologies and India's research priorities.
